scope: Open review abstract of superior sulcus (Pancoast) tumours: local invasion, historical survival, and trimodality treatment.

keyRecommendations.text: These tumours invade the apical chest wall and can involve the lower brachial plexus, ribs, vertebrae, subclavian vessels, or stellate ganglion, producing arm or shoulder pain or Horner syndrome.
They were originally considered universally fatal. Shaw and Paulson in 1956 combined radiotherapy and surgery, with 5-year survival of about 30%.
Trimodality treatment, induction concurrent chemoradiotherapy followed by resection, became standard in the 1990s, with 5-year survival up to 44% in the text.

clinicalBottomLine: A Pancoast tumour is an apical lung cancer that can cause arm or shoulder pain or Horner syndrome. Modern treatment in this review is induction chemoradiotherapy followed by resection.
notableCaveats: The PMC XML is essentially the abstract. Operative details and trial doses are not in the open text.
